instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of the basmati rice in a fine strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and a pinch of salt. Bring it to a boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.

Meanwhile, pick the fenugreek leaves off the stems and throw the stems away. Put the leaves in a large bowl of water, swish them around and lift them out. Repeat until the water is clear, then drain well. Chop the leaves roughly. That should be about 2 cups.

Finely chop the onions and tomatoes. Grate the ginger and mince the garlic. Cut the chicken into 1 inch pieces and toss it with 1/4 tsp of the salt. Slice the green chili thin and set it in a small bowl for the table.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the cloves, cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaf. After about 30 seconds they will sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the onions and cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden brown.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Turn the heat to low. Add the chili powder and turmeric and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the chicken right away and turn the heat to medium high. Stir for 4 minutes, until the outside is no longer pink.
Add the tomatoes, 1/2 cup water and the remaining 1 tsp salt. Cover, turn the heat to medium low and cook for 8 minutes, until the tomatoes have broken down into the sauce.

Stir in the garam masala, fennel, pepper and the fenugreek leaves. Cover and cook for 4 minutes, until the leaves are completely wilted. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the biggest piece. It's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the vinegar. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice, with the sliced green chili on the side.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes is the lead: whole spices in oil, onions browned, ginger and garlic, chili and turmeric, the chicken stir-fried, then tomato, garam masala and fresh fenugreek added last so the leaves don't turn bitter. Her curd is left out to keep the dish dairy-free; following her own reply to a reader, the tomatoes are doubled and a little vinegar goes in at the end for tang, with a splash of water for sauce. Piping Pot Curry and Fatima Cooks cook the same way with yogurt and more fenugreek. Fresh fenugreek can be hard to find; frozen leaves (use half) or dried kasuri methi would be the fallback. The honest time is about 41 minutes, over the 30 minute target.
